request.spec:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now move selected claims to another person in one go, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What's on screen** (`src/main/frontend/features/claims/reassign.slot.tsx`): a person select (`bulk-reassign-to`) and a "Move selected" button (`bulk-reassign`) next to the open and settle buttons. When it finishes it shows how many moved (`bulk-reassigned`) and how many were refused (`bulk-reassign-refused`). The counts disappear while a move is running, and the selection clears afterwards.

**On the server** there is a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-reassign`. It works through the selected claims in list order and puts each one through the same checks as moving a single claim: who may move it, its status, whether it's a correction, closed periods and retirement. Each claim that moves writes the same `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` and rollup lines as a single move. A claim that fails a check is counted as refused and left as it is.

**One rule differs from moving a single claim.** A single move refuses a claim that already belongs to the chosen person. The test expects the bulk version to accept it: it moves Ben's own claim "to Ben" and expects a `from=Ben to=Ben` record. So the bulk move skips that one check, controlled by a flag in `CheckReassign`. That makes it not quite "exactly the rules of moving one claim" as the request worded it.

**I also fixed an existing bug that the test hit.** The bulk open and bulk settle actions were ordering a person's claims by id rather than by how the list shows them. A claim that has just been moved to someone is listed as their newest, but these actions processed it in its old position. Claims were then numbered in the wrong order, which made scenario 3 fail. I changed bulk open, bulk settle and the new bulk move to use the list order, in `OpenClaims.java`, `SettleClaims.java` and `ReassignClaims.java`.
